Subject: Aurelia pilot: fitbench deep-dive, Redwood-verified profiles + next checkpoints

Ethan — great to meet you and Sofia this morning. Quick recap + what I promised to share after our call: 

1) Short summary of where we landed
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + answer surfacing (multi-turn, ~1.5–2k token context)
- Target QPS during pilot: 30–50 concurrent requests, burst to 100 for peak windows
- Primary success criteria: avg latency < 400ms p50 for 512-token responses; p99 < 1.2s; semantic quality on our prompt set >= 92% (A/B vs baseline)

2) Recommended models (Redwood-verified profiles attached + links)
- redwood-chat-13b-q4: best cost/latency balance for conversation throughput (recommended default)
- redwood-chat-34b-int8: higher-quality tier for tight SLAs on complex summarization tasks
- community-70b-llm (quantized variant): optional for edge-case generation where hallucination tolerance is lower

3) Performance highlights (links to full traces in Drive)
- Attached: redwood-aurelia-benchmarks.zip contains TPS matrices, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for the models above across 256/512/2048 contexts
- Topline: redwood-chat-13b-q4 @ batch=4 achieved ~900 TPS sustained on our dedicated pool for short prompts; p99 at 512 tokens ~0.9s in our EU region test—see latency-traces-20270322.json in the zip

4) Prompt sets & regression guardrails
- Attached prompt-set-v1.md: the seed prompts we used for quality checks and A/B. We recommend you run these as part of the pilot to validate semantic parity with your baseline.
- We'll also enable continuous prompt-level regression alerts tied to your pilot.

5) Next checkpoints / asks (proposed)
- Confirm pilot start date and scope (we recommend a 3-week pilot: week 1 ingest & smoke, week 2 quality tuning, week 3 load/power tests)
- Share a sample of redacted conversation logs (10–20 sessions) for prompt tailoring and warm cache prep
- Confirm any compliance needs (retention window, logs export, KMS requirement)

Attachments: redwood-aurelia-benchmarks.zip, prompt-set-v1.md

I'll be available to walk through the perf pack in a short call if you want — Karthik (SE) is looped for latency/runbook questions and Monica will coordinate the pilot SOW and timelines.

Thanks,
Rafael
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Ethan — quick technical notes to answer your latency/retention Qs and set expectations for the pilot: 

1) p99 at 2k token context (redwood-chat-13b-q4)
- Measured p99 (end-to-end) at 50 concurrent requests: ~1.05s (on dedicated pool, colocated in us-west region). We observe ~+0.15–0.25s variance under burst to 100 concurrent without autoscale bump. The p50/p95 were ~220ms / 480ms respectively for the same setup.

2) Network vs. generation split
- In our measurements ~70% of p99 is model generation; ~30% is networking and serialization when running over hosted API. Private deployments reduce network fraction significantly.

3) Tactical mitigations we recommend for your workload
- Enable prefix/KV caching for multi-turn sessions (reduces tokens generated per request by 15–35% depending on average session length)
- Use batching with max_batch=8 for high throughput windows (keeps tail latencies predictable while improving GPU utilization)
- Consider the redwood-chat-34b-int8 for the 10% of requests that require highest fidelity — can be routed via a canary policy to preserve cost.

4) Retention & export options
- Hosted default: 90-day retention for request logs, 30-day retention for unredacted traces is configurable on a per-customer basis. For the pilot we can set retention to 30 days and provide an S3 export hook for logs on demand. Encrypted-at-rest with KMS per your request.

5) Pilot plan and artifacts we can provide immediately
- Canary rollout doc and runbook (short): will attach data-handling-faq.pdf to the thread
- Latency traces: latency-traces-20270322.json (sample traces used in the perf pack)
- Post-pilot checklist for SLA evaluation and recommended rollout knobs

I'll be online for a technical sync on Thursday afternoon PST if you'd like to deep dive into the traces.

—Karthik
